tweet.text:
I told claude to create an initial specification document and gherkin scenarios based on my old Pharaoh game in C from the '80s.  Then I had it write the game in Clojure by using the C code as a reference.

This took quite a bit of fiddling because the scenarios were incomplete and so was the C source code (until I recovered the missing files).  

Once I had the game working in Clojure properly and was satisfied that it was covered well by scenarios, I moved the scenarios and the initial specification document to a fresh directory and instructed Claude to build the game in Javascript to be played on the web.

This worked tolerably well.  It took Claude three+ hours to build the game, and then took me another few hours to fiddle with it to deal with omissions and dumb UI errors.  

Overall, this was a good exercise.  Initial specs that describe wireframes and statics, and gherkin-like scenarios that describe dynamics are reasonably good at defining a project so well that Claude can build the project with only some minor issues.

I did not do mutation testing in this project.  But I'll be exploring that in projects to come.  I have hopes that it will constrain Claude's semantic variations even more tightly.
